# Yundera/AppStore — Radarr

**Audit date:** 2026-08-06 · **Store version:** `lscr.io/linuxserver/radarr:6.2.1` (running build 6.2.1.10461-ls310) · **Compose blob sha:** `26edb82f30b243a73dbe1e7ba5750bd02be67278` (last commit `0f5955e3e2`, 2026-07-10) · **Ref:** `main` · **Scope:** `n-a` (audit, no compose_base)

## Verdict

### NON-COMPLIANT · Critical · risk score 115

Radarr installs cleanly, works immediately, needs no manual configuration, and its data genuinely survives an uninstall→reinstall cycle. It is nonetheless **non-compliant**: on a fresh install the app is served on a public hostname with **no authentication gate at all**, and it hands its API key to any anonymous caller. Per the orchestrator Amendment §B.1, a Critical finding is unconditionally non-compliant.

**Finding counts:** 1 Critical · 1 Major · 5 Minor → `100·1 + 10·1 + 1·5 = 115` (triage only; the Critical alone decides the verdict).

---

## Functionality (Functional leaf `7HxjTwe63H`, strict full-run amendment)

**Demo host selected at runtime: **`demostaging2.inojob.com`**.** Both pool instances read `✅ Ready` on the Demo Management board; demostaging2 had **20.0h** Time Remaining vs demostaging1's **4.0h**, so demostaging2 was chosen (most remaining, comfortably > 1h). `🧹 Trigger Cleanup` was never clicked. Isolated context `functional-Radarr-audit`.

| Phase | Result | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **A — Session** | **pass** | Dashboard reached at `maison-demostaging2.inojob.com`. Password login was not needed: the Dex screen's **“Log in with Open Entry”** button authenticated passwordlessly. |
| **C — Fresh install** | **pass** | Store modal → card whose heading exactly matches `Radarr` → Install. Progress ran Downloading → `Starting… 15%` → installed tile. Correct app installed (no duplicate-modal mis-route). **Duration ≈ 75 s** (≤ 85 s wall clock, click → “Open” tile). No Tips dialog blocked the flow. |
| **D — Discover URL** | **pass** | Opening the tile yielded `APP_URL = https://radarr-demostaging2.inojob.com/`. |
| **E8 — Works immediately** | **pass** | Real Radarr UI within the bounded wait — Movies/Calendar/Activity/Settings nav, “No movies found…” empty state. No error page, no endless spinner, no “run this command / check logs” prerequisite. |
| **E9 — Auth gate** | ❌ **fail · Critical** | **No auth gate.** `GET /` returned HTTP 200 with the full UI and no redirect to any auth route; `/settings/general` also 200. `/api/v3/system/status` reported `"authentication": "none"`. `/initialize.json` served the API key anonymously, and that key granted HTTP 200 on `/rootfolder`, `/downloadclient`, `/indexer`, `/config/host` from an unrelated host. No `rationale.md` documents a public exception, so this is a FAIL, not a SKIP. |
| **E10 — Clean boot** | **pass** | `list_console_messages`: **0 first-party errors** (only signalR info/debug and two a11y advisories). `list_network_requests`: 38 requests, **no first-party 5xx** — every Radarr route 200. |
| **F — Zero-config usability** | **pass** | Reached a usable, secured state **purely in-browser**: set Authentication Method → *Forms (Login Page)*, created `audituser` + password, Save. No file edits, no shell, no container commands. Afterwards `GET /` correctly redirected to `/login?returnUrl=%2F` and `/initialize.json` returned 302. |
| **G — Data persistence** | **pass** | **Real uninstall → reinstall performed.** Uninstall (data kept: the platform renames the folder to `radarr.2026-08-06.archive`, compression left off), tile disappeared and the endpoint stopped serving. Reinstall via Install → restore menu → **“2026-08-06 folder”** (“Reinstalls the app on top of that backup's data and .env”). After it came up: `GET /` → `/login` (Forms auth preserved), the **pre-uninstall API key still valid** (same `config.xml` restored), and crucially `audituser`** logged in successfully** with the pre-uninstall password — `RadarrAuth` cookie issued, landing on the Radarr app — while a deliberate wrong-password control was rejected (`loginFailed=true`). User account, credentials and configuration all survived. |
| **G′ — Migration** | **n-a** | No `PRIOR_VERSION` supplied (audit runs a single current version) — the one input-forced `n-a` the amendment permits. |
| **H — Verdict & cleanup** | **pass** | See below. |

**Functional leaf verdict:** `not-functional` — mandatory Phase **E9** failed. Every other mandatory phase passed; no phase was skipped or errored.

### Note on the persistence mechanism

Phase G passed, but worth flagging for the platform rather than the app: this dashboard's uninstall does not leave data in place — it **renames** `AppData/radarr` to `radarr.<date>.archive`. Persistence therefore depends on the user picking the archive entry in the reinstall menu; choosing “Fresh install” silently starts empty while the old data lingers as an archive folder. The app's own mapping (`/DATA/AppData/radarr/config`) is correct and is what made the restore work.

---

## Cleanup

**Completed.** Radarr was uninstalled from `demostaging2.inojob.com` (tile ran `Archiving… 0%` → removed). The dashboard is back to its original four tiles (App Store, Maison, Settings, demo-auth) and `radarr-demostaging2.inojob.com` again falls through to the platform SSO. Residue outside my control: the platform-created `radarr.<date>.archive` folders under `AppData/` — the uninstall dialog offers no delete-data option, and removing them needs host access this sandbox does not have.

---

## Recommended remediation (highest value first)

1. **Close the auth hole (Critical).** Front Radarr with the AppShield OIDC sidecar (`ghcr.io/yundera/appshield`) as `Apps/ConvertX`, `Apps/Spliit` and `Apps/BrowserMCP` do, so the app is never reachable unauthenticated — including `/initialize.json`. If the first-launch-onboarding route is kept instead, it must at minimum not serve the API key to anonymous callers, and the API key should be rotated when auth is enabled.
2. **Add **`rationale.md`** (Major)** documenting whichever auth model is chosen, following the structure in `Apps/Stirling-PDF/rationale.md`.
3. **Minors:** add `--user $PUID:$PGID` to the `pre-install-cmd` user-directory creation; raise `cpu_shares` from `10` to `70` (consider doing it across the `*arr` family); add `PUID`/`PGID` to `environment:`; ship a real distinct `thumbnail.png`; add `x-casaos` per-volume and per-env descriptions.
